model_repository.repository_size: 3.61 GB including alternate epochs and sample audio

source_direct_findings: The primary model card identifies Thorsten-Voice/Kokoro as a German fine-tune of Kokoro-82M with approximately 82M parameters, a male Thorsten voice, local/offline use and an explicit CPU-friendly real-time-or-faster target claim.

The default checkpoint is epoch 5. The model card states that informal listening preferred epoch 5 over epoch 10 despite similar validation loss, so upstream scalar loss is not treated as Frankenstein listening-quality evidence.
The model card provides German edge-case samples covering umlauts, ich/ach sounds, eszett, numbers, prosody and technical terms such as API and JSON.
The German G2P path has a documented short-ue failure: misaki may emit U+028F (short ü), while the Kokoro vocabulary lacks that symbol; the provided inference path substitutes it with y.
Hyphenated German compounds may stumble at the hyphen boundary and very long sentences may be truncated; sentence splitting is recommended upstream.

The model repository uses .pth/.pt weight artifacts. The sample explicitly loads the voicepack with torch.load(..., weights_only=True); execution remains quarantined until exact runtime code/dependencies are pinned and inspected.
The model card pins semidark/misaki but leaves semidark/kokoro unpinned, creating a reproducibility/security gap that must be closed before any promotion-bearing runtime run.
project_inferences_not_runtime_facts: An 82M German male TTS candidate is a high-information CPU latency challenger against Piper/Thorsten and a potentially better fit for clay-direct-dev than multi-billion-parameter TTS candidates.
The fixed Thorsten acoustic identity aligns with the stable-male-voice invariant, but no Frankenstein identity/naturalness/ExpressionVector parity credit exists until actual audio is evaluated.
File-output synthesis is representable on the current CPU VPS even though audible playback and cancellation-to-silence are not; these scopes must remain separate.
counterhypotheses: CPU-friendly upstream claims may not reproduce under the exact 4-vCPU whole-Frankenstein resource envelope.
The G2P workaround may introduce pronunciation degradation or mask a more general vocabulary mismatch.
Piper/Thorsten may remain materially faster and more operationally deterministic despite lower subjective naturalness.
Kokoro may fail Frankenstein technical vocabulary, streamed chunk continuity or low-TTFA requirements even if complete WAV synthesis is fast.
